name: BREAK: Question Understanding Benchmark
description: BREAK is a question understanding benchmark comprising 83,978 questions across 10 diverse conversational and semantic parsing datasets. Questions are annotated with Question Decomposition Meaning Representation (QDMR), expressing complex questions as sequences of simpler computation steps.

license.name: MIT License (Code & QDMR Annotations) / Upstream Source Terms
license.notes: Code and QDMR annotations released under the MIT License by the Allen Institute for AI and Tel Aviv University. However, underlying questions originate from 10 diverse upstream datasets (including HotpotQA, DROP, Spider, ComplexWebQuestions, SQuAD 2.0, etc.) governed by heterogeneous open-access, share-alike, or restrictive licenses; commercial use of the aggregated benchmark is therefore subject to upstream source terms.

source_references.title: Break It Down: A Question Understanding Benchmark
source_references.notes: Published in Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics (TACL 2020).

verification.notes: Verified against TACL 2020 publication (DOI: 10.1162/tacl_a_00309) and official GitHub repository (allenai/Break). 83,978 total annotated questions partitioned across standard QDMR (60,150) and high-level QDMR (23,828) without double-counting; standard QDMR covers 10 source datasets while high-level QDMR addresses multi-hop databases and complex question subsets.
